svg.title: Order pipeline: from a click or an AI decision to the arrival executor
svg.desc: How an order travels: the player's click or the commander AI's $6822 write, the command slot $58016, the executor $6a3a / $6ac6, the three routes (run now, the dead direct branch $6b20, the carrier pigeon $4562), the pigeon's arrival $41dc clearing the pending word at $4220, the handler table $6b5a, the senders and the arrival executors, with the gate that proves each step. Sources: reversing/powermonger/strategy.md "The commander AI `$6522`" (queued orders, "The pending word"), "`$6822`: issuing an order", "`$6a3a` / `$6ac6` / `$6b38` the order executor", "The executor, proven", "What an AI invention order does", "The order senders and arrival executors, proven", "Transfer `$664c`, `$668c`" (k25: pigeon landed 6,279,910 steps later); reversing/powermonger/ai.md "`$4562` how an order reaches a subordinate captain" (routing, the dead direct branch, gate_pigeon_send.py), "The carrier-pigeon pool", "An arrival of another lord's pigeon" ($41dc). $4220 = clr.w -72(A0) inside the $41dc arrival block and $6b20 = clr.w -72(A1) checked by disassembly of scratchpad/pm123/win/m1_map.ram. Full fact list: order_pipeline.facts.md.
svg.text: Order pipeline: click or AI decision to arrival, and the pending word 4(group)
Box border = evidence for that step; the green line in a box names its gate. Each count is from the run or gate named in the box.
proven (callcap gate)
live (seen running)
code read
inferred
PowerMonger (Bullfrog / Electronic Arts, 1990) is a war game in which you give orders, not controls: the player picks an order icon (go,
attack, get men, take food and so on) and clicks a target on the map, and a captain's group walks there and acts. The computer lords
issue their orders through the same command slots and the same executor. The first captain's own group acts at once; an order for any
other captain is carried to him by a carrier pigeon and takes effect when it lands.
The figure follows one order from the click or the AI's decision to the routine that carries it out, and tracks the pending word
4(group): the field that marks a group whose order is still in the air, and which the commander AI reads as "do not decide for this
group".

The pending word 4(group) (array base + 4 + 2k = -72 from the group offset)
Set by $6822 for any group but the side's own. Cleared only at $4220 (pigeon
landing) and $6b20. While it is set, $6564 skips the group: no new decision.
Stuck words, a game bug after the side's first group dies:
$2776 frees the side's pigeons ($27c6), pending words stay set;
a new $4562 copies the dead sender's owner byte ($45a8), and
$3e06 skips a pigeon with owner <= 0 ($417a): it never flies.
py/arms/pending_census.py, 183 snapshots of live play, 357 set words: 70 pigeon in flight, 142 dead
sender, 141 no pigeon left, 4 queued; 4 with a live first group (strategy.md). Watch-proven on rand1_s1.
$6b38: clear type; types >= $34 exit; handler = $6b5a + word[$6b5a + type]
exec_census.py handler 32/32; live: 12 dispatches at $6b56 over 6 handlers (k60_s2)

$3956 (mode $74), $3da4 ($7a), $5fa0 ($22), in gate_orders.py

(4 issues); arrival 295k to 525k steps after $6c48 (22 of 22);

For the side's own group (D7 = 0) $6822 writes 4(group) := 0. A local $22 reaches $3ce8 only while $2df96 is set. Player order to a second captain, live (rand1.snap,
py/captain2/drive_order.sh): $3ce8 sets $58042[side] := $18a; the posture click launches $4562 (1 hit), counter $57fd8+2 goes 0 to 1, $41dc writes it back to 0
(at $4206) about 9.97M steps later, and $35a0 sets group 1's posture 3 to 2. Steps are emulator instructions.

svg.text: How to read it
Read top to bottom: boxes are the routines an order passes through and arrows the path it takes. Row 1 holds the two sources. $6822 writes an order
for the side's own group (the one $58042 names) straight into the side's command slot ($58016, one 6-byte slot per side); for any other group it
writes the order into the side record's header and sets the pending word. Every tick the executor $6a3a reads the slots and $6ac6 picks one of three
routes: run now (left), a direct branch that is dead in play (middle, dashed), or a carrier pigeon (right) that flies for millions of steps and, on
landing, clears the pending word and hands the order on. The routes meet at $6b38, which dispatches on the order type to a sender; the group's lead
then walks to the target, where an arrival executor finishes the order. The large blue box is the pending word and its bug.
Takeaway: the commander AI skips a group while its pending word is set, so an order that never flies freezes that group. When a side's first group
dies its pigeons are freed but the pending words stay set, and later orders copy the dead sender and never fly: of 357 set pending words in 183
snapshots of live play, 142 belonged to a dead sender and 141 had no pigeon.
Terms and evidence
Proven (callcap gate): the routine was rewritten in Python and run beside the game's own 68000 code, called in isolation from saved states with the
emulator's callcap command, and every changed byte matched; "1567/1567" is matching bytes out of bytes compared, "125 states" the saved states used.
Live: seen running in the emulator and counted. Code read: from the disassembly only. m1_s0, rand1, rand1_s1, k25 and k60_s2 are saved states of the
game (snapshots) that runs start from. Steps are emulated 68000 instructions. 4(group) is the pending word and 76(group) the state, in the AI's frame
(side base + 2k for group k); -72(A0) is the same pending word reached from the group offset.
